# A test run refuses an install that differs from package-lock.json

## Context

@tobiu, 2026-11-09: *"all peers should use npm i and ensure they use the latest playwright version. otherwise debugging is a different reality."* And: *"it is not just playwright, other dependency updates can have side-effects too."*

#20608 (11-08 21:23Z) moved `package-lock.json` to Playwright 1.65.0, which runs Chrome for Testing 158. CI installs exactly that. My clone kept 1.64.1 for hours afterwards, so every local "can't reproduce" that night ran a different browser than CI. `package-lock.json` changed 8 times on `dev` since 11-05. Fleet's Start reinstalls when a checkout's lockfile changed (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1480 / PR #1500), so the drift opens mid-session: a lock change merged after the session started stays uninstalled until the next Start.

## The Problem

Nothing tells a peer that their `node_modules` no longer matches `package-lock.json`. Tests, and the dev server, run quietly against whatever was installed last. A local result then speaks for another dependency set than CI's, and nothing in the output says so.

## The Architectural Reality

- npm writes its own record of the install to `node_modules/.package-lock.json` (the hidden lockfile). Comparing its `packages` with `package-lock.json`'s, by `version` and `resolved`, is exact. On a clean `npm i` at `6393c222a0`: 562 entries, 0 differences. 37 optional platform packages are absent by design, and there are no links or git dependencies.
- The eight Playwright configs (`test/playwright/playwright.config{,.component,.e2e,.matrix,.unit,.unit-tz,.update-chain,.visual}.mjs`) are standalone and reloaded in every worker and webServer process. Playwright never changes directory, so a check must locate the repository from its own file, not from `process.cwd()`.
- CI installs only through `npm ci` / `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which both write the hidden lockfile. Its two caches hold `~/.cache/ms-playwright` (keyed by Playwright version), never `node_modules`.
- `neo-agent-brain` already imports Engine helpers by path (`neo.mjs/buildScripts/util/sanitizer.mjs`; the Engine's `package.json` has no `exports`), so a helper in `buildScripts/util/` is reusable by Fleet.
- Design authority: n/a — no existing behavior is called wrong; this adds a guard for the operator's directive above.

## The Fix

- `buildScripts/util/check-installed-dependencies.mjs`:
  - `findInstallDrift(lock, installed)`, a pure comparison returning one line per package whose installed `version` or `resolved` differs from the lock, or which the lock requires and the install lacks. Linked entries, and missing optional, `devOptional` or peer entries, are skipped.
  - `assertInstallMatchesLock(root)`, which reads both files and throws, naming the packages and "run `npm i`". By default it checks the repository the file lives in.
  - A CLI entry that exits 1 on drift.
- Each Playwright config calls `assertInstallMatchesLock()` at load, so `npx playwright test -c …` stops before a worker starts.
- `package.json`: a `preserver-start` script runs the CLI, so `npm run server-start` (the dev server, and every Playwright webServer) refuses too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit spec pins `findInstallDrift`: a match, a version drift, a `resolved` drift, a missing required package, and the skipped link, optional, `devOptional` and peer cases.
- [ ] With Playwright installed off-lock (`npm i @playwright/test@1.64.1 --no-save`), `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs --list` fails, naming `@playwright/test`. After `npm i` it lists the tests.
- [ ] `npm run server-start` refuses on the same off-lock install.
- [ ] CI passes unchanged; its `npm ci` installs never differ from the lock.

## Out of Scope

- An automatic install on pull or checkout. Grace ruled it out on Fleet's surface (#1480's owner): a hook's `npm i` can rewrite the lock on a dependency branch and drop `npm link`s, and in a worktree whose `node_modules` is a symlink it rewrites the main checkout's packages under a running session. Count how often the check fires, then decide.
- Fleet's Start keying on this comparison instead of its receipt digest: Grace takes that on #1480's surface after the 13.4 cut, reusing the exported helper.
- Browser builds (Playwright already refuses a missing one), generated themes (`seat:start`), and globally installed tools.
